content: LYK5, also referred to as Protein Kinase LYK5 or STRADα, is a human protein encoded by the LYK5 gene. Function: Endogenous LKB1 and STRADα form a complex in which STRADα activates LKB1. This activation leads to the phosphorylation of both LKB1 and STRADα. The depletion of endogenous LYK5 through small interfering RNA (siRNA) disrupts the ability of LKB1 to induce G1 phase cell cycle arrest. STRADα stabilizes the LKB1 protein in both in vivo and in vitro conditions. When overexpressed alongside LKB1, STRADα can induce the formation of multiple axons in mouse embryonic cortical neurons. STRADα undergoes extensive splicing in vivo, and this splicing is regulated in a developmental and tissue-specific manner. However, the specific functions of the splice variants remain unclear. Disease Linkage: Mutations in the LYK5/STRADα gene are associated with a condition known as PMSE syndrome, which includes polyhydramnios, megalencephaly, and symptomatic epilepsy. Interactions: STRADα has been demonstrated to interact with LKB1 and MO25.
